turns.content: Hey! So I spent all Saturday going crazy over this baseline OD scatter in my succinate dehydrogenase assay — turns out the microcentrifuge tubes were warming up on the bench before the acid precipitation step 😅. Here's the excerpt from our method sheet about the 10% TCA precipitation in 50 mM phosphate buffer pH 7.4, spin at 4°C... I'm pretty sure the takeaway is that keeping tubes on crushed ice before spinning is critical to stop residual turnover, but the sheet's phrasing around pre-cooling the centrifuge is a little ambiguous. Does that match your read?

The method-sheet excerpt is not in the message, so I cannot evaluate its phrasing or whether it supports the crushed-ice interpretation.

Paste the relevant paragraph. Residual SDH activity is temperature-dependent until TCA denatures the protein; ice slows that residual turnover, and a 4 °C spin still requires a pre-equilibrated rotor. Whether the sheet actually says that remains unknown without the text.

Oh right, here's the excerpt — sorry, forgot to paste it 😅

"Add 500 µL ice-cold 10% TCA, vortex immediately, and incubate on ice 10 min. Centrifuge at 4°C, 12,000 × g for 10 min. Pre-cool rotor if necessary."

So the "pre-cool rotor if necessary" part is what threw me — but yeah, I think the ice incubation before the spin is doing the heavy lifting on stopping the reaction. Saturday was rough tracking down that scatter but honestly feels good to have nailed it to bench warming 🧊

The excerpt does not support that read.

Stopping the reaction is the ice-cold 10% TCA plus immediate vortex. The 10 min on ice is the precipitation hold after that quench. “Centrifuge at 4°C” and “Pre-cool rotor if necessary” only mean: run the spin at 4°C, and cool the rotor first if it is not already at temperature. That clause does not stop residual SDH turnover.

Bench warming **before** TCA is also outside this paragraph. The excerpt starts at TCA addition; it does not instruct holding tubes on ice up to that point. Residual activity until acid is mixed in is temperature-dependent, so that gap is consistent with the scatter you saw, but it is not what this text specifies.

If the method sheet should require ice from the end of the assay through TCA, that line is missing and would have to be written in separately.

Okay, so you're saying the quench is the TCA itself, not the ice hold? That actually makes more sense with the scatter pattern — the bench warm-up was eating into that window before TCA hit, not during the spin. Saturday was still the hard part though, confirming which pre-analytical variable broke the replicates 😅

Yes. The quench is mixing in ice-cold 10% TCA (immediate vortex). That denatures the enzyme. The 10 min on ice is the precipitation hold after the quench, not the stop. The 4 °C spin and “pre-cool rotor if necessary” only set spin temperature.

Residual SDH activity continues until TCA is mixed. Warm tubes in that window fit the scatter you described; this excerpt does not cover that window.

If the sheet should close it, add an explicit line: keep samples on ice from assay stop until TCA addition.

Alright, so Wednesday deadline means I re-run tomorrow with the ice step locked in. Does the spin timing change if the tubes are already precipitating on ice for the full 10 min? Or same 12k × g, same 10 min?

Same spin: 4 °C, 12,000 × g, 10 min.

The 10 min on ice is the precipitation hold after TCA. The spin pellets that precipitate. Completing the hold does not change g-force or spin time.

Keep samples on ice until TCA is mixed; that is separate from the spin and is not in the excerpt.
Alright, so same spin it is—good, less to re-optimize. I'll add that explicit ice step into my binder notes for Priya too so she doesn't hit the same Saturday wall 😅

Add this line, not a change to the spin:

Keep samples on ice from assay stop until ice-cold 10% TCA is added and vortexed.

Leave the rest as written: 10 min on ice after TCA, then 4 °C, 12,000 × g, 10 min (pre-cool the rotor if it is not already at 4 °C). That is the gap the excerpt does not cover.
